title: 〜(さ)せられる (causative-passive)
meaning: be made to… / be forced to… (often with reluctance)
simpleExplanation: The causative-passive combines "make someone do" and "be done to": 食べさせられた "I was made to eat". The person who was forced is the subject; the person who forced them takes に. It usually carries a feeling of reluctance or complaint: 一時間も待たされた "I was kept waiting a whole hour".
whenUsed: Complaints about bosses, seniors, parents (飲まされた, 働かされた), and also to describe being moved emotionally: 考えさせられる映画 "a film that makes you think". Common in both speech and writing.
formation: Group 1: -aせられる, or the short form -aされる (書く → 書かせられる / 書かされる)
Group 1 verbs ending in す: only the long form (話す → 話させられる)
Group 2: -させられる (食べる → 食べさせられる)
する → させられる / 来る → 来させられる
Structure: (forced person) は (forcer) に Verb-させられる

branches.label: causative-passive (long form): be made to drink
causative-passive (short form): be made to drink

examples.ja: 子供の頃、母に野菜を食べさせられた。
examples.reading: こどものころ、ははにやさいをたべさせられた。
examples.en: As a child, I was made to eat vegetables by my mother.
examples.note: Group 2: 食べ + させられる. Forcer marked with に.

examples.ja: 先輩にお酒を飲まされた。
examples.reading: せんぱいにおさけをのまされた。
examples.en: I was made to drink by my senior.
examples.note: Short form of Group 1: 飲まされる.

examples.ja: 一時間も待たされて、腹が立った。
examples.reading: いちじかんもまたされて、はらがたった。
examples.en: I was kept waiting a whole hour and got angry.

examples.ja: 新人の頃は、毎日遅くまで残業させられた。
examples.reading: しんじんのころは、まいにちおそくまでざんぎょうさせられた。
examples.en: When I was new, I was made to work overtime late every day.
examples.note: する verb → させられる.

examples.ja: この本を読んで、命の大切さについて考えさせられた。
examples.reading: このほんをよんで、いのちのたいせつさについてかんがえさせられた。
examples.en: Reading this book made me think about how precious life is.
examples.note: Emotional use: 'was made to think' with no unpleasant nuance.

similarGrammar.difference: From the forcer's viewpoint: 母は私に野菜を食べさせた. The causative-passive flips it to the victim's viewpoint.
Something is done to you (叱られた). The causative-passive is being made to do something yourself.
'Have no choice but to' — obligation from circumstances, not from a person (N2).

commonMistakes.why: Verbs ending in す do not take the short form; 話さされる is incorrect.

commonMistakes.wrong: 母は私に野菜を食べさせられた。
commonMistakes.right: 私は母に野菜を食べさせられた。
commonMistakes.why: The subject must be the person forced; the forcer takes に.
Order is causative first, then passive: させ + られる.

usageNotes: The short form (書かされる, 待たされる) is very common in speech; the JLPT accepts both.
The emotional use with 考える, 感動する, 驚く (感動させられた) expresses being deeply affected.
Compare the three: 食べさせる (make eat) / 食べられる (be eaten, can eat) / 食べさせられる (be made to eat).
jlptTips: Identify who is forcing and who is forced; the forced person is the subject of させられる.
For す-verbs the short form does not exist, so 話さされる in the choices is always wrong.
Keywords like 無理に, 嫌々, 一時間も point to the causative-passive.
